QC report — img_syn2x01

1. Verdict

img_syn2x01 is most consistent with Batch 2 (probability 1.00; Batch 1: 0.00; Batch 3: 0.00; assignment stable in 100 % of strip-bootstrap resamples; confident). It sits -2.0 σ along Batch 1's signature (Si-candidate number density ↑, crack density ↑, Si-candidate loading ↑) and +5.8 σ along Batch 2's signature (pore correlation length ↑, pore anisotropy ↑, Si-candidate D50 ↑). It lies further from the Batch 2 centroid than any labelled image, but in Batch 2's own signature direction: a more extreme Batch-2-like sample rather than a new kind of variation. Relative to the Batch-3 baseline it is different from the baseline — verdict REJECT: 9 of 16 KPIs exceed 2.5 robust σ. Largest shifts: pore correlation length 66.3 px vs 45.4 px ± 2.27 (z = +9.2); pore anisotropy 2.65 vs 1.83 ± 0.092 (z = +8.9); Si-candidate D50 7.40 µm vs 4.78 µm ± 0.308 (z = +8.5). Reads as: longer in-plane pore correlation length; pores more aligned parallel to the collector: higher through-plane tortuosity, slower fast charge; consistent with heavier calendering. Baseline has 4 image(s), so the smallest reportable rank p-value is 0.200; this verdict is an effect-size judgement, not a significance test.

4. Drivers (shortlist, sorted by |z|)

  • pore correlation length (s2_len_pore_h_px, class R): 66.3 px vs 45.4 px ± 2.27, z = +9.22 (higher) — longer in-plane pore correlation length
  • pore anisotropy (aniso_pore_chord_ratio, class R): 2.65 vs 1.83 ± 0.092, z = +8.90 (higher) — pores more aligned parallel to the collector: higher through-plane tortuosity, slower fast charge; consistent with heavier calendering
  • Si-candidate D50 (si_d50_aw_um, class R): 7.40 µm vs 4.78 µm ± 0.308, z = +8.47 (higher) — coarser Si-candidate (area-weighted D50): higher fracture and swelling risk, more particle isolation
  • in-plane pore chord (pore_chord_h_mean_um, class R): 2.31 µm vs 1.66 µm ± 0.083, z = +7.76 (higher) — wider in-plane pores
  • carbon/flake anisotropy (aniso_carbon_chord_ratio, class R): 2.40 vs 1.81 ± 0.091, z = +6.48 (higher) — graphite/carbon more aligned parallel to the collector: higher through-plane tortuosity; consistent with heavier calendering
  • deep-pore fraction (pore_frac_deep, class W): 11.77 % vs 14.51 % ± 0.73 %, z = -3.77 (lower) — less deep porosity (lower bound): denser coating, slower ionic transport; consistent with heavier calendering
  • crack density (crack_density_um_per_mm2, class M): 2,883 µm/mm^2 vs 7,331 µm/mm^2 ± 1,548, z = -2.87 (lower) — fewer cracks
  • Si-candidate/pore contact (si_contact_pore_frac, class R): 2.37 % vs 4.23 % ± 0.67 %, z = -2.77 (lower) — less buffer space around Si-candidate: swelling stresses the matrix

7. Not measurable from these images

coating thickness, surface roughness, collector delamination, binder/carbon-black distribution, Si vs SiOx identity, true (total) porosity.

Caveats

  1. Bright particles are identified by backscatter Z-contrast only (no EDS); they are reported as Si-candidates and may include SiOx or Si-C composite.
  2. Pores appear open (not resin-infiltrated); the deep-pore fraction is a lower bound on porosity, not a porosity measurement.
  3. Graphite, carbon black and binder cannot be separated in these images; the 'carbon matrix' class contains all three.
  4. Coating thickness, surface roughness and collector delamination are not assessable: the fields lie entirely inside the coating.
  5. Anisotropy and transport indices are 2-D section quantities compared like-with-like against the baseline, not 3-D values; the through-plane direction is assumed vertical in the frame.
  6. Pixel size (25 nm/px) is taken from the TIFF resolution tags; vendor metadata is absent, so it is unverified.
  7. With N baseline images the smallest achievable rank p-value is 1/(N+1); verdicts are effect-size judgements against a small baseline.
  8. Image grey levels have been remapped after acquisition (comb histograms); any method relying on raw intensities would be confounded - this system uses BSE phase identity after smoothing and treats ETD/InLens levels as acquisition covariates.

Notes: sample is in the labelled set; it was held out of the baseline and the centroids for this evaluation
